title: A real UI for watching and steering agents
body:
grogu watch today is a one-shot text board or a redraw loop (-f). Neither is how a swarm actually gets supervised: the user wants to see agents appear, spot one stuck, and steer it without composing a CLI command.

Requirements taken from use:
- who is running, on which plan, and how long idle
- open defects and escalations that are waiting on the user specifically
- steer a named agent in one keystroke, without retyping ids
- should not require keeping a terminal focused

Options to weigh: a TUI with per-agent rows and an inline steer prompt; a small local web dashboard; or system notifications plus the existing board. Note that steering delivery is now push-first (plan steer names the running agents so the spawner relays with write_agent), so a UI should relay the same way rather than only writing notes.

Follow-up to the agent-pipeline branch (PR #31).

log.text: A real UI for watching and steering agents

Considered A2A (Agent2Agent, v1.0 since Mar 2026, Linux Foundation, 150+ orgs) as the transport for steering and inter-agent comms. Decided against for now: A2A explicitly does not support interrupting a task in the 'working' state -- a client sends input only once the agent enters 'input-required'. That is the same wall write_agent hits, so it would not reduce steering latency at all, while adding HTTP endpoints on the machine that holds iMessage/Gmail/keys. Grogu's roles also do not communicate conversationally by design: defects, amendments and gates are a shared state machine with adjudication, which is deliberately stronger than exchanging messages.

Worth borrowing without adopting the wire protocol: A2A makes 'input-required' a first-class task state. grogu watch shows 'waiting on you' only buried inside a per-plan block. The UI should hoist a single 'blocked on you' section to the top -- approvals, escalations and open amendments across all plans -- so supervision is one glance rather than a read.

Triggers that would flip the A2A decision: wanting a non-Copilot agent in the pipeline (cloud coding agent, vendor agent), agents on another machine, or Grogu's roles being callable by another harness.
